milestones.title: First Paid Pour
milestones.text: After years of reading about spirits and cocktails, Joshua began taking private bartending work in the Portland area. His first paid event was a birthday party where a battered Plymouth Duster carried him, his bar tools, and considerably more confidence than experience into the beginning of what would become roughly fifteen years behind the bar.

milestones.title: Learning the Room
milestones.text: Private events grew into professional bar work and years spent learning the realities of hospitality: speed, consistency, guest service, inventory, high-volume service, and how to read a room. Those years provided the practical foundation underneath everything that came later.

milestones.title: Wedding Volume
milestones.text: At Oregon City's Abernethy Center, Joshua worked a demanding schedule of weddings and private events, sometimes serving crowds ranging from roughly 50 to 500 guests. The volume sharpened the kind of organization and composure that only comes from doing the work repeatedly.

milestones.title: Finding the Craft
milestones.text: A deeper interest in classic cocktails and serious cocktail bars changed the direction of the career. What had begun as a job became a subject of study: spirits history, dilution, balance, presentation, service, technique, and the small details that separate a drink from a well-made drink.

milestones.title: Bar Institute
milestones.text: Joshua attended Bar Institute in consecutive years, studying advanced bartending and bar-management subjects while becoming more involved with Portland's professional bartending community. These events helped turn years of practical experience into a more deliberate professional education.

milestones.title: Whiskey Education
milestones.text: At Neat Whiskey Bar in Portland, Joshua worked with a back bar containing more than 350 unique spirits. The role became an intensive whiskey education, from tasting and product knowledge to creating drinks from a guest's flavor description rather than simply handing them a menu.

milestones.title: Behind the Business
milestones.text: At a Portland Irish pub, Joshua advanced from bartender into bar management. His responsibilities expanded into cocktail development, inventory, ordering, staff training, opening and closing procedures, events, and menu work. He also developed a whiskey club that helped increase customer interest in the category.

milestones.title: The Gordon House
milestones.text: On October 27, 2017, Joshua participated in a cocktail competition and fundraiser connected to Frank Lloyd Wright's Gordon House in Oregon, representing his bar with an original presentation built around Irish whiskey and smoke. The event was an important step from creating drinks during service to putting his work in front of an industry audience.

milestones.title: Building Drinks, Not Just Making Them
milestones.text: Cocktail development became increasingly systematic. Whiteboards, flavor families, ingredient testing, cost considerations, and menu structure became part of the process. Drinks including Ruby Queen, In a Pickle, The Metropolitan, Major Moses, and other original builds document a period when creativity became a serious part of the job.

milestones.title: Tales of the Cocktail
milestones.text: Joshua traveled to New Orleans for Tales of the Cocktail, taking coursework focused on whiskey, hospitality, and emerging non-alcoholic drinks. He also received his first Fernet-Branca coin, one of those small industry traditions that means considerably more to bartenders than it does to almost anyone else.

milestones.title: World Class Studios
milestones.text: Preparing for Diageo World Class pushed the technical side of the craft further: fermentation, sustainability, preservation, carbonation, Brix measurement, highballs, sensory science, and advanced ingredient preparation. It was some of the most concentrated cocktail education of Joshua's career.

milestones.title: Birds of Paradise
milestones.text: Years of experimentation came together in Birds of Paradise, built around Johnnie Walker Gold and a house clove infusion. Surviving development photographs show the drink moving from experimentation to the final presentation that became his World Class entry.

milestones.title: Diageo World Class Top 100
milestones.text: Joshua's work earned him a place in the Diageo World Class Top 100 in 2019, the clearest professional recognition of a career spent studying spirits, developing drinks, and continuously trying to get better behind the bar.

milestones.title: Taking It Forward
milestones.text: By the end of 2019, Joshua began transitioning away from active bartending. The bar career ended, but the skills did not: hospitality became cooking and hosting, cocktail development became broader flavor work, and years spent telling stories across a bar eventually became writing, video, and creative work.
